title: Hats, hoods and crowns
notes: King Karl has his hair again, drawn back into a bun, and wears a proper crown: a gilt band set with stones, eight pearl-tipped points and a cross over red velvet.
Hats and hoods across the realm now sit on people's heads, not at their mouths or necks; hoods cover the head with no hair poking through.
The minstrels' harp is held lower so you can see the harpist, and the recorder player holds the recorder below her chin.

title: The throne hall rebuilt
notes: King Karl's throne hall is rebuilt in warm Romanesque stone: round arches on thick pillars, an open oak roof, amber glass, torches and iron wheels of candles.
The king's minstrels play old hymns beside the throne: harp, hurdy-gurdy, lute, recorder and frame drum.
King Karl now truly sits on his throne — a carved oak throne with velvet padding, gilt lions' heads and a footstool.
The Royal Guards' helms now sit properly over their heads.
The guards stand at their posts and look about the hall; the king shifts and looks around from his throne; the minstrels play their instruments in time with the music.
Each village's banner is now its own battle-worn shield on the pillars, in the village's colour with the crest of the realm in gold and its sign embroidered round the edge.
A shield stays under a dark cloth until you cleanse that village's chapel; the next time you enter the hall, the cloth falls away.

title: The launcher
notes: Kingdom's Last Knight now has a launcher for Windows, Mac and Linux: play offline, update when you choose.
Back up, restore and export your saves. A backup is made before every update.
Installed on a Chromebook, the game keeps your version until you tap Update.

title: The beasts' heads
notes: Every pelt's head is reshaped: bear, wolf, fox, lion, stag, ram and raven, with jaws, noses, eyes, ears, antlers and horns.
With the hood down, the head rests on top of a shield slung on your back.

title: Pelts that move as one
notes: Pelts and hoods are one soft piece that moves with your shoulders: no more coming apart when you run.
Animal hoods wear a short cape hung diagonally from the left shoulder.
With the hood down, the beast's head hangs behind your neck.

title: A sturdier shield
notes: The shield stays on your forearm in every pose, keeps its full shape on your back and faces square when you block.
You can walk while blocking.

title: Boots and greaves
notes: Thicker boots and shoes; trousers tuck in under greaves.
Capes and cloaks lie under a shield on your back.

title: Legs & boots
notes: One Legs & boots choice: each set brings its own, plus common kits — trousers and boots, barefoot, armoured legs with steel or leather boots.

title: Gloves
notes: Gloves come with your vambraces and bend with your fingers: plated, leather, fur-cuffed, decorative, fingerless and wraps.

title: Armour that stays put
notes: Armour no longer loads messy or comes loose when you move or attack.
